analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: the 'Last updated' date (line 3), the performance_measurements row at line 578, and a new paragraph at lines 580-586. The new text says sample_age_ms is measured from the newest observation, even if an older completed observation arrives later. It also says the Swift producer applies this rule per workload bucket and current-posture series (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.observe), keeps the receipt-order EWMA and sample counts, and leaves wire fields unchanged. This is documentation of routing-telemetry freshness only. It adds no message type, field, authorization path, key handling or encryption change. The text states the wire is unchanged, so TB-002 and TB-011 boundaries are not affected. The performance_measurements fields remain provider-reported and untrusted. The coordinator treats them as routing measurements and clamps them elsewhere, which is outside the supplied evidence. The wider doc still correctly describes the endpoint-resumption controls (4 KiB strict codec, single reply on the originating socket, no local trust grant, T-053 binding) and the drain barrier; these lines were not modified. The Swift implementation of the age rule and the Go coordinator's handling are not in this batch, so the claimed producer behavior is unverified, but no security conclusion depends on it. No threat-model update is needed.
